heroHeadline: Marcos Confirms 'Provisional Understanding' With China on Sierra Madre Resupply as DFA Defends RORE Arrangement Against Carpio Criticism; Beijing Issues Sandy Cay Ecological Report Blaming Manila
heroSubtitle: President Marcos told foreign correspondents in Manila on August 14 that a 'provisional understanding' with Beijing governs BRP Sierra Madre resupply missions to Second Thomas Shoal, while insisting Manila is not seeking China's permission or ceding sovereignty; he also said joint oil-and-gas exploration talks with China had 'moved forward' amid Middle East-driven oil-price volatility. The Department of Foreign Affairs and AFP spent August 7-14 repeatedly defending the Provisional Understanding on Rotation and Resupply (RORE) — 15 incident-free missions to date — against retired Justice Antonio Carpio's warnings that it risks Philippine sovereign rights under the 2016 Arbitral Award. Separately, China's Ministry of Natural Resources published its first comprehensive ecological bulletin on disputed South China Sea reefs on August 14, reporting live coral coverage at Sandy Cay near Thitu Island down roughly 70% since 2016 and blaming Philippine construction and fishing activity. The report follows a week of Washington-Beijing sparring over China's 'nature reserve' designation at Scarborough Shoal, which the US State Department has called a destabilizing pretext for territorial control, and early-August PLA amphibious/bomber drills near the shoal.
